lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read introduces a short narrative about weekend plans and reported speech, helping students understand future intentions (“I’m going to…”) and changes in plans through a contextualised story.
Look for students following the text while listening, identifying the characters’ plans, recognising why the plans changed, and showing comprehension by answering simple questions about the story.

“Maybe I can write a story about a fun weekend. I really want to see a play. Can you help me get some ideas? I know! There’s Minh and Kevin! What do you think their weekend plans are? Let’s read and follow along to find out!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - A Read and number.

details: Read and number strengthens understanding of story sequencing by having students identify the correct order of events using familiar sentences from the text.
Look for correct numbering, careful reading, matching each paragraph to the right order, and showing clear understanding of the story sequence.
“The story is mixed up! Let’s read each part and decide the correct order of events from the weekend.”

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.77 - B Read and circle T/F

details: Read and circle T/F checks understanding of the story by identifying correct and incorrect information using simple true-or-false statements.
Look for correct choices, careful reading of each statement, and match ideas to the story accurately.
“I think these sentences are about Minh and Kevin, but I’m not really sure. Let’s read them together to see which sentences are true or false.”

“Let’s look at some more weekend activities. Help me find the correct words so we can read what the people did.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - B. Choose and write the correct answer

details: Choose or write the correct answers checks detailed comprehension of the reading as students identify characters’ intentions, actions, and reasons.
Look for correct choices based on the story, meaningful written answers using key details, and students pointing to the line in the text that supports their answer.
“Sometimes plans don’t work… I said I was going to see a play, but I didn’t! Minh and Kevin made weekend plans, but not everything went as planned. How can we find out more?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - C. Write and share

details: Write and share practises the target structure “I’m going to…” as students write about their own weekend plans, their friend’s plans, and chores they can do to earn money.
Look for complete answers using “I’m going to…”, correct verb forms, clear idea sentences, and confidence in sharing plans with a partner or class.
“Now it’s your turn. What are you going to do this weekend? What is your friend going to do? And if you need money like Kevin, what chores could you do?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - C Make your own story.

details: Make your own story encourages creativity and controlled use of reported and future forms as students write a simple narrative using given prompts and pictures.
Look for logical sequencing of events, correct use of “I’m going to…” and time expressions, and short, meaningful sentences that match the pictures.
“We’ve seen Minh and Kevin’s weekend story. Now let’s write our own story using the pictures to show what someone planned and what they did.”
